SUBJ-automation-reproducibility.name: Automation, Scripting, and Reproducibility
SUBJ-automation-reproducibility.summary: Workflow automation and reporting practices for transparent and repeatable analyses.
learning_goals: Package analyses into reproducible, shareable workflows.

SUBJ-domain-applications.name: Domain Applications
SUBJ-domain-applications.summary: Applied case studies connecting method choices to biological interpretation.
learning_goals: Integrate end-to-end workflow decisions in realistic biological studies.

SUBJ-feature-extraction-quantification.name: Feature Extraction & Quantification
SUBJ-feature-extraction-quantification.summary: Translation of segmented objects into measurable biological descriptors.
learning_goals: Extract robust features and understand feature sensitivity.

SUBJ-image-data-formats.name: Image Data & Formats
SUBJ-image-data-formats.summary: Standards and metadata practices for interoperable and reproducible bioimage analysis.
learning_goals: Adopt consistent data organization and QC checks.

SUBJ-imaging-foundations.name: Imaging Foundations
SUBJ-imaging-foundations.summary: Microscopy and signal-formation concepts required to reason about image quality and downstream analysis.
learning_goals: Connect imaging physics to analysis reliability.
Identify acquisition choices that affect quantitative outcomes.

SUBJ-machine-learning-bia.name: Machine Learning in BIA
SUBJ-machine-learning-bia.summary: Foundational ML concepts and caveats specific to bioimage analysis tasks.
learning_goals: Understand data needs, validation, and bias for ML segmentation.

SUBJ-preprocessing.name: Preprocessing
SUBJ-preprocessing.summary: Core correction and enhancement steps before segmentation and quantification.
learning_goals: Choose preprocessing methods matched to noise/artifacts.

SUBJ-segmentation-detection.name: Segmentation & Object Detection
SUBJ-segmentation-detection.summary: Classical and modern approaches to identify biological structures in images.
learning_goals: Evaluate segmentation quality with objective metrics.

SUBJ-statistics-experimental-design.name: Statistics & Experimental Design
SUBJ-statistics-experimental-design.summary: Statistical reasoning for reliable interpretation of image-derived measurements.
learning_goals: Match statistical tools to experimental questions.
Design experiments with appropriate controls and sample size.

TOP-background-correction-and-flat-field.title: Background Correction and Flat-Fielding
TOP-background-correction-and-flat-field.summary: Illumination and background correction methods for robust quantification.
learning_outcomes: Select correction approaches for uneven illumination/background.
Assess correction side effects on biological signal.

TOP-basic-wave-optics.title: Basic Wave Optics for Microscopy
TOP-basic-wave-optics.summary: Wave optics concepts needed for understanding diffraction and resolution.
learning_outcomes: Explain diffraction and numerical aperture in practical terms.
Connect optical constraints to measurable image quality.

TOP-bioimage-file-formats-and-metadata.title: Bioimage File Formats and Metadata
TOP-bioimage-file-formats-and-metadata.summary: File format ecosystems and metadata essentials for reproducible BIA.
learning_outcomes: Inspect metadata needed for quantitative analysis.
Recognize interoperability pitfalls across tools.

TOP-classical-segmentation-methods.title: Classical Segmentation Methods
TOP-classical-segmentation-methods.summary: Watershed, region growing, edge-based and morphology-based segmentation methods.
learning_outcomes: Select classical segmentation methods for common object types.
Tune parameters while minimizing bias and manual overfitting.

TOP-data-management-and-quality-control.title: Data Management and Quality Control
TOP-data-management-and-quality-control.summary: Dataset organization, naming, versioning, and QC checkpoints for BIA projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply a consistent folder and metadata strategy.
Define QC checkpoints before and after preprocessing/segmentation.

TOP-deconvolution-basics.title: Deconvolution Basics
TOP-deconvolution-basics.summary: Conceptual and practical introduction to deconvolution in fluorescence microscopy.
learning_outcomes: Explain when deconvolution can improve interpretability.
Recognize artifacts introduced by poor PSF assumptions.

TOP-denoising-classical-methods.title: Denoising: Classical Methods
TOP-denoising-classical-methods.summary: Gaussian, median, non-local means and related denoising methods with parameter trade-offs.
learning_outcomes: Choose denoising filters based on noise assumptions.
Avoid oversmoothing structures of biological interest.

TOP-domain-case-study-cell-biology.title: Domain Case Study: Cell Biology Quantification
TOP-domain-case-study-cell-biology.summary: End-to-end cell biology case study integrating acquisition-aware processing and quantitative interpretation.
learning_outcomes: Assemble an end-to-end BIA workflow for a realistic cell biology question.
Justify method choices and discuss uncertainty transparently.

TOP-experimental-design-controls-and-pow.title: Experimental Design, Controls, and Power
TOP-experimental-design-controls-and-pow.summary: Planning robust BIA experiments with controls, replication, and power considerations.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate technical vs biological replication in imaging studies.
Plan control conditions and sample sizes for expected effect sizes.

TOP-feature-extraction-morphology-intens.title: Feature Extraction: Morphology, Intensity, Texture
TOP-feature-extraction-morphology-intens.summary: Derivation of interpretable quantitative features from segmented objects.
learning_outcomes: Extract morphology, intensity, and texture features reproducibly.
Identify feature confounders linked to acquisition and preprocessing.

TOP-image-registration-basics.title: Image Registration Basics
TOP-image-registration-basics.summary: Rigid/non-rigid alignment fundamentals for time-lapse and multi-channel data.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish rigid and non-rigid registration use cases.
Evaluate registration quality and failure cases.

TOP-imaging-artifacts-and-bias.title: Imaging Artifacts and Measurement Bias
TOP-imaging-artifacts-and-bias.summary: Common artifacts (bleaching, drift, shading, saturation) and bias prevention strategies.
learning_outcomes: Identify artifacts that confound biological interpretation.
Design checks to detect and mitigate bias early.

TOP-intro-bioimage-analysis.title: Introduction to Bioimage Analysis
TOP-intro-bioimage-analysis.summary: Scope, goals, and common workflows in quantitative bioimage analysis.
learning_outcomes: Describe the typical BIA pipeline from acquisition to interpretation.
Recognize common failure modes that impact biological conclusions.

TOP-microscopy-modalities-overview.title: Microscopy Modalities Overview
TOP-microscopy-modalities-overview.summary: Survey of widefield, confocal, spinning disk, and light-sheet modalities and their analysis implications.
learning_outcomes: Compare strengths and limitations of major microscopy modalities.
Relate modality choice to downstream preprocessing and segmentation needs.

TOP-ml-segmentation-overview.title: ML-based Segmentation Overview
TOP-ml-segmentation-overview.summary: Practical overview of supervised deep-learning segmentation workflows and caveats.
learning_outcomes: Describe training/validation/testing splits for segmentation models.
Recognize data bias and domain-shift risks in biological imaging.

TOP-noise-models.title: Noise Models in Bioimaging
TOP-noise-models.summary: Photon, read, and background noise models and their impact on analysis.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate key noise sources in microscopy data.
Use noise characteristics to motivate preprocessing choices.

TOP-ome-data-model-and-standards.title: OME Data Model and Standards
TOP-ome-data-model-and-standards.summary: OME concepts and practical use for managing microscopy metadata consistently.
learning_outcomes: Explain core entities in the OME data model.
Use OME-compatible outputs in analysis workflows.

TOP-pixel-size-and-sampling.title: Pixel Size and Sampling
TOP-pixel-size-and-sampling.summary: Sampling theory basics (Nyquist, aliasing) for microscopy images.
learning_outcomes: Compute whether sampling is adequate for a target resolution.
Identify undersampling and oversampling trade-offs.

TOP-psf-and-resolution.title: Point Spread Function (PSF) and Resolution
TOP-psf-and-resolution.summary: PSF, diffraction-limited resolution, and consequences for analysis quality.
learning_outcomes: Explain PSF and diffraction-limited resolution.
Relate resolution limits to segmentation and quantification uncertainty.

TOP-segmentation-quality-metrics.title: Segmentation Quality Metrics
TOP-segmentation-quality-metrics.summary: Metric-based evaluation of segmentation outputs and annotation agreement.
learning_outcomes: Compute overlap and boundary-based quality metrics.
Interpret metric values in context of downstream biological decisions.

TOP-statistical-testing-and-effect-sizes.title: Statistical Testing and Effect Sizes
TOP-statistical-testing-and-effect-sizes.summary: Statistical testing, confidence intervals, and effect size reporting for image-derived data.
learning_outcomes: Select statistical tests based on assumptions and design.
Report effect sizes and uncertainty alongside p-values.

TOP-thresholding-and-binarization.title: Thresholding and Binarization
TOP-thresholding-and-binarization.summary: Global and local thresholding approaches as entry-level segmentation tools.
learning_outcomes: Apply global and adaptive thresholding appropriately.
Diagnose under- and over-segmentation from threshold choices.

TOP-workflows-scripting-and-reproducibil.title: Workflows, Scripting, and Reproducibility
TOP-workflows-scripting-and-reproducibil.summary: From GUI pipelines to scripted workflows with provenance and version control.
learning_outcomes: Automate repeatable workflows for batch analysis.
Capture provenance and version information for reproducible reporting.

PATH-bia-for-biologists.name: BIA for Biologists
PATH-bia-for-biologists.summary: Application-first pathway with bridge support for optics, statistics, and scripting.
outcomes: Design and run a reproducible BIA workflow for cell biology questions.

PATH-bia-for-computer-scientists.name: BIA for Computer Scientists
PATH-bia-for-computer-scientists.summary: Method-focused route with bridges in microscopy physics and experimental design.
outcomes: Implement acquisition-aware and biologically valid analysis pipelines.

PATH-bia-for-physicists.name: BIA for Physicists
PATH-bia-for-physicists.summary: Builds on strong quantitative background and emphasizes biological assay context and interpretation.
outcomes: Translate quantitative imaging expertise into biologically grounded analysis decisions.
